issues.what: The follow-up's central multiplicity claim is wrong: it reports that the revised harness.spa excluded no candidate on either timeframe because 'every grid variant's selection gain is non-zero in every active session (no variant applies the Foundation's next-CHoCH exit, so every variant differs from the benchmark wherever a session has a trade)', and therefore that the studentised SPA p is unchanged. In fact the exclusion rule is inert for this family because harness.spa counts a session as active when |gain| > 1e-9, and the lab.manage replay prices an exit identical to the L1 label with ~1e-5 to 5e-3 INR of arithmetic noise (the study's own grid check only asserts 'net within 0.005'). The near-benchmark variants the previous refuter flagged are therefore still in the studentised family and still inflate the bootstrap null. The reported studentised SPA p-values (minute 0.396 / 0.3965, 5-minute 0.4965 / 0.4825) are artefact-inflated; the pass-rule verdict does not flip (corrected p still > 0.10 and the top-1%-removed item fails independently), so the null result survives, but the numbers, the 'excluded candidates: none' statement and the explanation in section 10.2 are incorrect and the item the follow-up was tasked to fix is not fixed.

Then: the per-session |gain| values split cleanly into pricing noise (max 0.00528 INR on minute, 0.00487 on 5-minute) and genuine exit differences (min 0.0104 and 0.0374). Every one of the 1568 variants has at least one noise-only session; the harness counts all 1568 as active in 578/578 (408/408) sessions. Variant 1177 (stop foundation / scale none / trail none / time_stop None / choch True) on 5-minute has gains [812.53, 0.0049, 0.0048, ...]: genuinely active in 1 of 408 sessions (min-active threshold 20); variant 1183 (same + inert 120-bar time stop) is identical. On minute variant 1177 has gains [85.58, 76.98, 64.60, 55.95, 50.81, 35.74, 0.59, 0.0049, ...]: genuinely active in 7 of 578 (threshold 28). In the studentised bootstrap null these degenerate candidates are the argmax in 37.7% of the 2000 draws on 5-minute (19.7% on minute); the median null max drops from 2.61 to 1.68 (5-minute) when they are excluded. Recomputing harness.spa's arithmetic with the same draws and recentring but excluding candidates with fewer than min_active sessions of |gain| > 0.01 INR: minute family RC p 0.501 -> 0.448, SPA p 0.396 -> 0.322 (best still 785, t 1.683); minute all-trials 0.3965 -> 0.314; 5-minute family RC p 0.5175 -> 0.21, SPA p 0.4965 -> 0.185 (best still 1025, t 2.761); 5-minute all-trials 0.4825 -> 0.1685. harness.py:474-480's docstring states the exclusion exists precisely to remove such near-zero-variance candidates ('the exit-policy refuter's finding'), so the revision's intent was not realised.

issues.what: The follow-up's SPA re-run did not remove the near-benchmark variant it was meant to remove. FINDINGS states '0 of 1568 candidates excluded ... every grid variant's selection gain is non-zero in every active session (no variant applies the Foundation's next-CHoCH exit, so every variant differs from the benchmark wherever a session has a trade)'. That is true only at the harness's 1e-9 INR activity threshold: the variant `stop foundation / scale none / trail none / time_stop None / choch True` is, in substance, the Foundation L1 exit (the next CHoCH after an entry is always against the position), and its per-session selection gain exceeds 0.05 INR in only 7 of 578 sessions (minute, exit-ledger id 0c142743f6d7b0bd) and 1 of 408 (5minute, id ea2c65c77b1f3eda; its inert-key twin `time_stop 120`, id 807549ccd89a4d42, is identical). The other sessions carry |gain| ~ 1e-3 INR: float noise between lab.manage's arithmetic and l1_net_inr (the parity check tolerates 0.005 per trade), which the 1e-9 test counts as 'active'. So the studentised SPA p reported in sections 3, 9 and 10 (0.396 minute, 0.4965 5minute; all-trials 0.3965 / 0.4825) is still inflated by exactly the candidate the harness revision targeted, and the stated reason for '0 excluded' is false.
